sections.title: 🟢  EASY
sections.body:
Five minutes of prep or less. No pilot, no specialist, no editor, and every one of them runs at four people on a dead Tuesday. If you have never hosted, start here.

Press an op below for its full brief: setup, phases, roles, what wins it and what goes wrong.

sections.title: 1  FIRST CALL
sections.body:
> PvE · 4 to 6 players · 60 min

The game writes the op. The host queues one mission from the FOB tablet and reads the objective list, so prep is about five minutes and the night ends on a mission complete banner rather than on the host's judgement. It is the easiest mission in the game, it has no prerequisites, and it pays credits and EXP, so a bad night still leaves everyone better off. This is the op you bring a stranger to.

**Op card**
```
OP FIRST CALL // PvE // Pushkino
PvE, 60 min, 4 to 6. Pushkino crew recovery, the easiest mission in the game, no
prerequisites. Bring a breaching charge from the armory. We come in on the northeast
road. Pays credits and EXP. Good night to bring a friend. RSVP on the buttons by
18:00.
```

sections.title: 2  HOLD THE LINE
sections.body:
> PvE · 4 to 8 players · 60 min

One location, one clock, one call from the host. He says the wave direction and nothing else, so he can host it off a phone while playing. It ends on the clock rather than on a wipe or a capture, which means it never overruns and never leaves people standing around. Sectors are assigned before anyone moves, so two bad players cannot lose it for everybody.

**Op card**
```
OP HOLD THE LINE // PvE // Kozlovka
PvE, 60 min, 4 to 8. We take one building on the edge of Kozlovka and hold it for
twenty minutes against reinforcement waves. Sectors assigned before we move. Nobody
pushes deeper and nobody chases outside the wire. Ends on the clock, not on a wipe.
```

sections.title: 3  FOUR MINUTE HOUSE
sections.body:
> Training · 4 to 8 players · 60 min

Zero prep, zero tooling, one stopwatch, and a number written in the thread at the end. The FOB Killhouse gives a free dry rep with no AI and no travel, which is where the stack order actually gets fixed. It is the drill that makes every other op faster, and it is the cheapest hour of hosting on the list.

**Op card**
```
DRILL // Four Minute House // CQB
Training, 60 min, 4 to 8. Room clearing. One dry rep in the FOB Killhouse, then three
live reps at Kozlovka, Pushkino and Depot. Rifle, one flash, one charge, no launchers.
Stack lead rotates so everyone leads once. Standard is a block cleared under four
minutes with no downs.
```

sections.title: 8  BOUND AND COVER
sections.body:
> Training · 4 to 8 players · 60 min

The cheapest drill on the list and the one that fixes the single worst habit a teenage roster has, which is everybody sprinting at once. The host walks behind and counts faults out loud. It needs no mission, no editor, no pilot and no specialist, and it runs at four people on a dead Tuesday.

**Op card**
```
DRILL // Bound and Cover // Movement
Training, 60 min, 4 to 8. Fire and movement. Two pairs cross five hundred metres of
open ground into Kozlovka in bounds. One pair moving, one pair stopped and shooting,
never both. Two crossings. Score is double move faults and the second crossing has to
be zero.
```

sections.title: 9  STOPWATCH
sections.body:
> Training · 3 to 6 players · 60 min

Stealth in this game is a published numbers system and nobody joins knowing any of it. Three runs at one village turn the numbers into something a fifteen year old can feel, and the measured output is a distance a rangefinder reads out loud, so there is nothing for the host to judge. It needs no editor, so the session still pays, and it is the gate before anyone goes on SILENT LADDER.

**Op card**
```
DRILL // Stopwatch // Stealth numbers
Training, 60 min, 3 to 6. Stealth at Lesdolina, done wrong on purpose and then done
right. Bring a rangefinder. We measure the range you get spotted at: standing, then
prone, then prone through dead ground. Nobody goes on a stealth op before doing this.
```
